# cubewarden

> cubewarden keeps a Magic: The Gathering cube balanced against rules its designer writes: for the whole cube,
> for each colour and for each archetype. Open source (MIT): https://github.com/sinsimon/cubewarden

## For agents using this page (browser)

The page exposes `window.cubewarden`, the same operations as the command line:

- `cubewarden.check()`: rules and mechanics not met (`failing` = primary, `warnings` = secondary).
- `cubewarden.explain(id)`: a rule's value, target and the cards behind it.
- `cubewarden.search(filter, { scope, sort, limit, source })`: cards outside the cube that match; only cards the cube's
  "every card" rules allow. `sort`: `cubes` (default: most used on CubeCobra), `elo`, `picks`, `wr`, `wrraw`, `mv`, `name`.
  `source: "maybeboard"` looks only at the cards kept aside (all of them, whatever the "every card" rules say).
  With a colour or archetype as `scope`, the filter can use `member:<mechanic id>`, `member:any`, `member:primary`,
  `member:secondary` (that scope's mechanics); without a scope `member:` is an error. Once the project's reference
  cubes have loaded, each card carries `refs` (how many of them play it) and the result `refsOf` (how many loaded).
- `cubewarden.tryChanges({ add: [names], remove: [names] })`: effect of a swap on every rule, nothing saved.
- `cubewarden.applyChanges({ add, remove })`: make the swap; the page saves and redraws. `add: ["Make Your Move (FDN)"]`
  or `"Make Your Move (FDN) 143"` adds the card in that printing.
- `cubewarden.changes()`: adds and removes against the imported list, new maybeboard cards and printing changes
  (`printings`), with a changelist for CubeCobra.
- Printings: each cube or maybeboard card is shown and exported (CSV: set, collector number) in one printing; the card
  itself (rules, filters, win rates) does not change with it. `cubewarden.printings(card)` lists the printings the card
  data has, the allowed sets first; `cubewarden.setPrinting(card, set, number?)` switches it, e.g.
  `setPrinting("Make Your Move", "fdn")`. With an "every card" set rule (`every(s:fdn,tmt)`),
  `cubewarden.printingIssues()` lists cards shown outside those sets and `cubewarden.useAllowedPrintings()` switches
  them all (or `useAllowedPrintings([names])` some) to an allowed printing: the set their win rate comes from, else
  the newest allowed set.
- `cubewarden.maybeboard({ add, remove })`: cards kept aside (CubeCobra's maybeboard), listed with no arguments;
  `applyChanges({ remove, toMaybeboard: true })` moves cut cards there. They are not counted by any rule.
- `cubewarden.rules()`, `cubewarden.setRule({ id, name, scope, text, priority })`, `cubewarden.removeRule(id)`.
- `cubewarden.mechanics()`, `cubewarden.setMechanic({ id, name, scope: "color:W" | "archetype:<id>", text, priority })`,
  `cubewarden.removeMechanic(id)`: the "musts" of a colour and the mechanics of an archetype (a mechanic counts cards).
- `cubewarden.syntax()`: the filter and rule syntax. `cubewarden.help()`: this list.

Where the browser supports WebMCP (`document.modelContext`), the same operations are registered as tools named
`cubewarden_check`, `cubewarden_explain`, `cubewarden_search`, `cubewarden_try_changes`, `cubewarden_apply_changes`,
`cubewarden_rules`, `cubewarden_set_rule`, `cubewarden_mechanics`, `cubewarden_set_mechanic`, `cubewarden_changes`,
`cubewarden_maybeboard`, `cubewarden_printings`, `cubewarden_set_printing`, `cubewarden_printing_issues`,
`cubewarden_use_allowed_printings`, `cubewarden_syntax`.

Ask the person before `applyChanges`, `setPrinting`, `useAllowedPrintings`, `setRule` or `removeRule`: they change
the cube they are working on.

## For agents in a terminal

Run `cubewarden help`. The project is two files: `cubewarden.json` (rules + card list) and `cards.json`
(card data). `cubewarden check --json` exits 1 when a primary rule is not met. `cubewarden serve` opens this page
on those files; after that the page keeps its own copy in the browser. To hand work between the page and the
terminal, use Changes → "Download project file" and "Open project file".

## Rule syntax (short)

- Filters: `otag:removal t:creature kw:flying mv>=4 spellmv<=2 c=wu c<=wu c=scope is:hybrid s:fdn,trk wr>=1.5 wrraw>=55% cubes>=1000 tag:"UG Ramp" member:any`, with `or`, `( )`, `-`.
- `spellmv` compares every mana value a card can be cast for as a noncreature spell, and matches when any of them
  passes: its own mana value, the spell side of an adventure, omen or prepared creature, each half of a split card,
  kicker (each and both), multikicker (one kick), tiered (each tier), spree (all modes), entwine, and the costs of
  flashback, harmonize, beam me up, escape, mayhem, overload, foretell, cleave, sneak, web-slinging, warp, madness,
  miracle, surge. `count(spellmv<=2)` counts cheap spells, `count(spellmv>=5)` big ones. An X spell matches any
  `>=`/`>` and `<=`/`<` from its X=0 cost. Creatures without a spell side and lands never match (`-spellmv>=0`
  finds them). Scryfall has no such filter: "Open in Scryfall" leaves it out and says so.
- Win rates (17Lands): `wr` is the WR Δ, in percentage points: the card's adjusted WR (GIH WR minus the strength of
  the decks it was played in) minus the average adjusted WR of its set's commons and uncommons. `wr>=1.5` = 1.5 points
  above an average common or uncommon, `wr<0` = below it; cards from different sets compare. Pages show it signed
  (`+3.0`, `−1.2`). `wrraw` is the raw GIH WR in percent (`wrraw>=55%`); `wr>=55%` is an error.
- Rules: `count(F) >= 6`, `count(F) in 13..14`, `count(t:creature) >= 50%`, `count(c=scope -is:hybrid) = 3 fixed`,
  `avg(wr, member:any) in 1..3.5`, `every(s:fdn,trk)`, `every(mv, t:creature) <= 5`.
- Mechanics are named filters; the numbers live in rules. In a colour or an archetype, `member:<mechanic id>` matches
  the cards of that scope's mechanic, `member:any` any of its mechanics, `member:primary` / `member:secondary` by
  priority: `count(member:removal) >= 4`. In an `allColors` or `allArchetypes` rule, `member:<id>` uses each scope's
  own mechanics (a scope without that id matches no card).
  A mechanic's target is the rule of its scope that counts exactly that mechanic, `count(member:<id>) >= 10`: the page
  shows and edits the two as one row. To set a target from code, `setRule` that rule (`setMechanic` keeps the filter).
- Curves: `curve(t:creature) 1:1..3 2:5..7 3:4..6 4:2..4 5:1..3 6+:0..2` (a target per mana value; `6+` = 6 and above,
  `0:` = zero-drops), `curve(t:creature) 2:20%..30% 3:15%..25%` (percent of the filtered cards),
  `curve(-t:land) 1-2:8..12 3-4:6..9 5+:2..4` (a bucket over a range of mana values: `1-3` = 1, 2 or 3; buckets must
  not overlap, only the highest can be `+`). Counts scale like `count()`, `fixed` at the end does not. `check()` and
  `explain(id)` return `buckets: [{ label, value, target, status }]`, with labels like `2`, `1–3`, `6+`.
  A bucket is `near` when it is one card off: within 1 of a count target; for a percent target, moving one filtered
  card into or out of the bucket (the total unchanged) reaches the range. The rule is `near` when every miss is.
- Scopes: `cube`, `color:W` … `color:G`, `color:C` (colourless nonland), `color:L` (lands), `archetype:<id>`, `allColors`, `allArchetypes`.

CubeCobra has no write API: changes go back as a changelist or a CSV the person uploads, and rules travel in a
hidden line at the end of the cube's About text (`[cubewarden-v1]: cw:…`).
